identity.name: GRASIM INDUSTRIES LTD
identity.industry: Decorative Paints & B2B Building Materials E-Commerce

summary.oneLiner: Grasim transformed into a multi-engine growth platform with Birla Opus achieving 100% revenue growth and 10% market share in decorative paints, while Birla Pivot more than doubled revenue; profitability remains secondary to market share gains, but structural cost advantages and capacity scaling are setting up margin expansion in FY27-28
summary.business: Grasim Industries, the Aditya Birla Group flagship, manufactures Cellulosic Staple Fibre and Fashion Yarn, chlor-alkali and specialty chemicals, and building materials -- cement (via subsidiary UltraTech Cement), decorative paints (Birla Opus) and a B2B e-commerce platform for building materials (Birla Pivot). It also holds a majority stake in diversified financial services (Aditya Birla Capital) and runs smaller textiles, renewables and insulators businesses. Customers span the textile value chain, industrial and institutional chemical users, construction/infrastructure buyers, retail paint consumers and MSME contractors, across India and over 90 countries.

Chemicals: Specialty Chemicals (epoxy polymers and curing agents)

currentContext.strengths: India's largest caustic soda producer with a pan-India presence across the chlor-alkali segment|Leadership position in the domestic Cellulosic Staple Fibre market with exports to over 50 countries|Integrated Cellulosic Fibres model anchored by captive dissolving-grade pulp from Harihar and scale advantages across four manufacturing sites|Diversified portfolio across Cellulosic Fibres, Chemicals, Building Materials and Financial Services that lets cycles naturally balance out, shielding consolidated profitability|Birla Opus paints network is backward integrated with in-house emulsions (376.5 MLPA) and resin (92.6 MLPA) manufacturing; commissioning of the sixth factory cut average logistics cost by over 30%|Birla Opus R&D scale -- 14 dedicated labs at Taloja with a team of 100+ experienced scientists supporting portfolio expansion and cost leadership|Track record as Aditya Birla Group flagship: revenue CAGR of 16% and total shareholder return of 15%+ over the last decade
currentContext.strategies: R&D across opex and capex is treated as a strategic priority in Cellulosic Fibres, focused on pioneering fibre platforms (Lyocell, specialty, circular fibres), premiumisation, and process innovation for cost reduction, reliability and sustainability|Strengthening in-house engineering capabilities for faster lab-to-plant scale-up, supported by dedicated pilot facilities, specialised hardware, advanced modelling/testing, and partnerships with global technology providers, brands and value-chain partners|In Chemicals, scaling downstream and Specialty businesses beyond the chlor-alkali foundation to drive higher value creation through integration, cost leadership and sustainable operations|Continuing to expand into higher-value downstream products across Caustic Soda, Chlorine Derivatives and Epoxy, deepening integration and increasing captive consumption of intermediates, progressively shifting the portfolio toward a more resilient, value-added Specialty Chemicals platform|Building a differentiated portfolio of sustainable chemistries anchored by Green Epichlorohydrin (ECH), increasing renewable energy usage, and Recyclamine (R) technology for wind-blade recycling, to strengthen positioning in low-carbon and circular-economy markets|FY 2026-27 priorities in Cellulosic Fibres: optimise product mix, drive operational efficiencies, and execute capacity expansions, while maintaining cost discipline and elevating the value-added product portfolio through R&D|The Board recommended a dividend of 500% (Rs 10 per equity share of face value Rs 2), to be put to shareholder vote at the 79th AGM on 21st August 2026. No broader capital-allocation, balance-sheet or reinvestment philosophy statement is present within this governance/entity-structure excerpt of the Annual Report.
currentContext.expansion: Cellulosic Fibres: expanding Lyocell capacity at Harihar, Karnataka by a combined 165K TPA -- an existing 55K TPA expansion plus a newly approved 110K TPA tranche backed by more than Rs 3,000 crore of additional investment -- taking total Lyocell capacity to 210K TPA by 2030; the business also targets overall CSF capacity of ~1 million TPA by 2028 with a higher share of specialty fibres. Building Materials (Paints, Birla Opus): commercialised its sixth and largest plant at Kharagpur in October 2025, completing a pan-India network of 6 plants with total capacity of 1,332 MLPA (~24% of organised decorative paints industry capacity), backward integrated with in-house emulsion (376.5 MLPA) and resin (92.6 MLPA) manufacturing; FY26 capex of Rs 550 crore took cumulative project spend to Rs 9,902 crore, completing the greenfield build-out on time and without cost overrun; retail presence scaled via Birla Opus Paints Gallery to 1,200+ franchised stores across 700+ towns. Building Materials (Cement): group subsidiary UltraTech Cement crossed 200 MTPA total grey cement capacity in April 2026 (up from ~52 MTPA in 2011), becoming the world's largest cement company outside China, through a mix of organic expansion, acquisitions and operational focus. B2B E-commerce (Birla Pivot): platform build-out to 50,000+ SKUs sourced from over 1,000 leading Indian and global brands, with expanding logistics, lender and procurement partnerships. Group level: total consolidated capital expenditure of Rs 15,396 crore in FY26 with growth capex comprising 72%, following nearly Rs 74,000 crore invested across businesses over the preceding five years; a strategic capital commitment of Rs 2,880 crore was made to financial services subsidiary Aditya Birla Capital. Chemicals: inaugurated a new CPVC Resin facility during the year (detail truncated in source text).
currentContext.mdna: Global Cellulosic Fibre consumption expected to grow 3-4% YoY, led primarily by robust Lyocell demand growth of about 28% YoY, even as broader cellulosic fibre demand stays flat|China accounts for 65-70% of global CSF consumption and production, so its operating rates and inventory levels are key drivers of CSF pricing; conditions remain resilient in China but stressed in Turkey, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Indonesia due to high rates, weak FX and US tariff pressure on exports|India's cellulosic fibre consumption expected to grow faster, aided by GST harmonisation at 5% across the value chain for garments priced below Rs 2,500|Cellulosic fibres, especially Lyocell, are positioned to bridge the gap left by cotton (water scarcity, volatile output, rising land costs) and polyester (fossil-fuel origin, microplastic concerns), underpinning long-term growth potential|India's cellulosic fibre business is expected to average a 9.76% annual growth rate to reach US$3 billion by 2033, with gradual normalisation of inventory cycles supporting a steady demand recovery; near-term margin volatility may persist due to import alternatives|Chemicals: FY 2026-27 likely to remain volatile due to geopolitics, but medium-to-long-term outlook remains constructive on steady demand growth and gradual normalisation of global supply-demand dynamics; consistent execution on cost, utilisation and portfolio mix expected to improve cycle-end competitiveness|Caustic soda demand driven by rising alumina consumption linked to electrification and renewable energy, plus steady demand from textiles, specialty chemicals, pulp & paper, and soaps & detergents|Chlorine derivatives demand supported by water treatment and disinfection (Jal Jeevan Mission), wider Zero Liquid Discharge adoption, industrial growth, rising water stress, and steady growth in agrochemicals and infrastructure|Specialty Chemicals (Epoxy) see strong structural demand from wind energy, e-mobility, and infrastructure-led industrial applications; India's expanding FTA network (UK, UAE, Australia, EFTA) and ongoing India-EU trade negotiations enhance export opportunities|Domestic chlor-alkali industry utilisation remained around 80%; despite healthy demand growth in FY 2025-26, domestic realisations broadly tracked softer global pricing trends, resulting in stable volumes but moderated pricing growth|Birla Opus: FY 2025-26 was an inflexion year for the decorative paints industry with heightened competitive intensity and one large-scale acquisition by a recent entrant; Birla Opus revenue and volumes grew over 100% YoY with more than 3% revenue market-share improvement, and its distribution network (50,000+ dealers, 146 depots, 11,500+ towns) became the industry's 2nd largest

risks.note: Management explicitly flags that intensifying competition could reduce market share and pressure margins; mitigation relies on expanding capacity to retain share and investing in brand equity through R&D, quality, cost efficiency, delivery and customer service.

Disruptions along key maritime corridors during the year increased transit times and reduced supply-chain reliability, compounded by heightened security concerns and rerouting requirements that added cost and complexity to global operations; named as a distinct category (Inherent and Residual) on the Company's own risk heat map.
Energy and commodity markets remained volatile through the year, driven by geopolitical tensions, directly affecting input costs for Grasim's energy- and commodity-intensive manufacturing businesses.
Named explicitly on the Company's risk heat map as both an inherent and a residual risk, relevant given export exposure (9% of turnover) and cross-border operations/sourcing.

Named explicitly on the Company's risk heat map as both an inherent and a residual risk, relevant to a capital-intensive group carrying debt across its manufacturing and financial-services businesses.

Named explicitly on the Company's risk heat map as both an inherent and a residual risk to operations, alongside supply chain, currency and interest-rate risk, reflecting physical and transition exposure of Grasim's manufacturing footprint.

The Company flags an increasing use of tariffs, policy interventions, and evolving regulatory frameworks across the geographies it operates in and exports to, even though it notes the impact on Grasim has so far been limited with the broader operating environment staying largely stable.

Cyber security is explicitly listed by the Board as one of the material risk categories systematically identified and assessed across the organisation, alongside strategic, financial, operational, compliance and knowledge-based risks.

one-line thesis: Grasim transformed into a multi-engine growth platform with Birla Opus achieving 100% revenue growth and 10% market share in decorative paints, while Birla Pivot more than doubled revenue; profitability remains secondary to market share gains, but structural cost advantages and capacity scaling are setting up margin expansion in FY27-28
financial scorecard: revenue: +18% CAGR FY21-26 (consol. INR1,75,431cr); EBITDA/margin: Paints EBITDA improved but margin compressed by 20-25% input cost inflation; PAT (rptd): INR4,000cr dividend inflow from UltraTech; PAT (normalized): Excluding one-off dividend, core EBITDA up 15% in cellulosic, 55% in renewables; order book: Birla Pivot: 5,000+ pin codes, 5,000+ retail touchpoints; net debt: INR2,880cr invested in Aditya Birla Capital to maintain 52.3% stake
guidance: revenue growth: Paints: high double-digit FY27; Birla Pivot: on track to hit INR8,500cr annual guidance; margin: Paints margin to recover post-price hikes; order inflow: Birla Pivot expanding steel, bitumen, polymers; capex/commissioning: Capex guidance for FY27 to be shared next quarter; Kharagpur paint plant (Oct 2025) fully operational
order book & pipeline: Birla Pivot: 5,000+ pin codes, 5,000+ retail touchpoints, 45,000+ institutional paint sites pipeline; Birla Opus: 70+ govt specs approved, 1,200+ exclusive retail outlets
segment / subsidiary detail: Paints: Q4 revenue +52% YoY (like-for-like), +71% ex-CWIP; FY26 revenue doubled; market share +370 bps to ~9.7%; 50k dealers, 146 depots, 37k tinting machines, 1,200+ retail outlets, 3,000+ AID partners; 42 new products launched; 65% premium mix; 75% product superiority in blind tests; Birla Pivot: Q4 revenue >2x YoY; 5,000+ pin codes; expanding into steel, copper, polymers; integrated OS with embedded finance; Cellulosic Fibres: Q4 revenue INR4,614cr (+14% YoY), EBITDA INR588cr (+2x YoY); FY26 EBITDA up 15%; Lyocell Phase 1 (55k TPA) progressing; Chemicals: Chloralkali capacity 1.5M TPA; caustic soda sales 321k tons Q4; Specialty chemicals 27% of revenue; Cement: UltraTech 200M TPA capacity (world’s largest outside China); EBITDA/ton INR1,253; Financial Services: Aditya Birla Capital raising INR4,000cr; Grasim investing INR2,880cr to maintain 52.3% stake
growth verticals / optionality: Birla Opus: 15k+ towns target by FY27; 10,000cr revenue target in 3rd year of full ops (FY28); PaintCraft service expansion to 6,000+ pin codes; Birla Pivot: scaling embedded finance for MSMEs; new categories (steel, copper, aluminum); cellulosic fiber: Phase 2 Lyocell expansion (110k TPA total); chemical: downstream specialty chemicals growth; financial services: India’s financialization tailwind
margins & cost dynamics: Paints: COGS up 20-25% due to crude-linked raw materials and INR depreciation; price hikes implemented (Jan-Mar 2026, additional in Apr 2026); 10% free paint promotion retained; EBITDA margin compressed but recovery expected in H2 FY27; Cellulosic: EBITDA up 15% on benign pulp prices and mix shift; Chemicals: Specialty chemicals margin pressured by ECH input costs; Cement: EBITDA/ton INR1,253 (highest ever) due to fuel/logistics efficiency
capex / expansion: Kharagpur paint plant (INR1,500cr+) commissioned Q3 FY26; Lyocell Phase 2 capex pending; Birla Pivot tech infrastructure scaling; UltraTech capex largely complete; FY27 capex guidance to be shared next quarter
capital allocation: INR4,000cr dividend from UltraTech; INR2,880cr reinvested in Aditya Birla Capital to maintain 52.3% stake; final dividend of INR10/share (500%) paid; remaining cash used for growth capex in paints and Pivot; no share buybacks announced
risks & watch-items: Raw material inflation (20-25% COGS increase) persisting; demand elasticity testing in H1 FY27; price hikes may slow contractor adoption; Birla Pivot’s unit economics still early-stage; regulatory risk in financial services; currency volatility; geopolitical disruption to crude/pulp supply
management quality / tone: Confident, ambitious, disciplined; strong focus on market share over short-term profitability; emphasis on long-term structural advantages (distribution, brand, integration); acknowledges inflation risks but remains bullish on India’s growth; tone is ‘calibrated optimism’
non-obvious takeaways: Birla Opus’s 75% product superiority in blind tests is a hidden moat; PaintCraft’s 6-12 month EMI service is a defensible financial innovation; Birla Pivot’s integration with Grasim’s supply chain (cement, chemicals, metals) is an unreplicable moat; contractor loyalty via Opus ID app creates sticky ecosystem; 90%+ unaided brand recall in 2 years is unprecedented in Indian paints

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Grasim Industries, the Aditya Birla Group flagship, manufactures Cellulosic Staple Fibre and Fashion Yarn, chlor-alkali and specialty chemicals, and building materials -- cement (via subsidiary UltraTech Cement), decorative paints (Birla Opus) and a B2B e-commerce platform for building materials (Birla Pivot). It also holds a majority stake in diversified financial services (Aditya Birla Capital) and runs smaller textiles, renewables and insulators businesses. Customers span the textile value chain, industrial and institutional chemical users, construction/infrastructure buyers, retail paint consumers and MSME contractors, across India and over 90 countries.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: Paints: high double-digit FY27; Birla Pivot: on track to hit INR8,500cr annual guidance; margin: Paints margin to recover post-price hikes; order inflow: Birla Pivot expanding steel, bitumen, polymers; capex/commissioning: Capex guidance for FY27 to be shared next quarter; Kharagpur paint plant (Oct 2025) fully operational

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Birla Opus: 15k+ towns target by FY27; 10,000cr revenue target in 3rd year of full ops (FY28); PaintCraft service expansion to 6,000+ pin codes; Birla Pivot: scaling embedded finance for MSMEs; new categories (steel, copper, aluminum); cellulosic fiber: Phase 2 Lyocell expansion (110k TPA total); chemical: downstream specialty chemicals growth; financial services: India’s financialization tailwind

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global Cellulosic Fibre consumption expected to grow 3-4% YoY, led primarily by robust Lyocell demand growth of about 28% YoY, even as broader cellulosic fibre demand stays flat
- China accounts for 65-70% of global CSF consumption and production, so its operating rates and inventory levels are key drivers of CSF pricing; conditions remain resilient in China but stressed in Turkey, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Indonesia due to high rates, weak FX and US tariff pressure on exports
- India's cellulosic fibre consumption expected to grow faster, aided by GST harmonisation at 5% across the value chain for garments priced below Rs 2,500
- Cellulosic fibres, especially Lyocell, are positioned to bridge the gap left by cotton (water scarcity, volatile output, rising land costs) and polyester (fossil-fuel origin, microplastic concerns), underpinning long-term growth potential
- India's cellulosic fibre business is expected to average a 9.76% annual growth rate to reach US$3 billion by 2033, with gradual normalisation of inventory cycles supporting a steady demand recovery; near-term margin volatility may persist due to import alternatives
- Chemicals: FY 2026-27 likely to remain volatile due to geopolitics, but medium-to-long-term outlook remains constructive on steady demand growth and gradual normalisation of global supply-demand dynamics; consistent execution on cost, utilisation and portfolio mix expected to improve cycle-end competitiveness
- Caustic soda demand driven by rising alumina consumption linked to electrification and renewable energy, plus steady demand from textiles, specialty chemicals, pulp & paper, and soaps & detergents
- Chlorine derivatives demand supported by water treatment and disinfection (Jal Jeevan Mission), wider Zero Liquid Discharge adoption, industrial growth, rising water stress, and steady growth in agrochemicals and infrastructure
- Specialty Chemicals (Epoxy) see strong structural demand from wind energy, e-mobility, and infrastructure-led industrial applications; India's expanding FTA network (UK, UAE, Australia, EFTA) and ongoing India-EU trade negotiations enhance export opportunities
- Domestic chlor-alkali industry utilisation remained around 80%; despite healthy demand growth in FY 2025-26, domestic realisations broadly tracked softer global pricing trends, resulting in stable volumes but moderated pricing growth
- Birla Opus: FY 2025-26 was an inflexion year for the decorative paints industry with heightened competitive intensity and one large-scale acquisition by a recent entrant; Birla Opus revenue and volumes grew over 100% YoY with more than 3% revenue market-share improvement, and its distribution network (50,000+ dealers, 146 depots, 11,500+ towns) became the industry's 2nd largest

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Paints: COGS up 20-25% due to crude-linked raw materials and INR depreciation; price hikes implemented (Jan-Mar 2026, additional in Apr 2026); 10% free paint promotion retained; EBITDA margin compressed but recovery expected in H2 FY27; Cellulosic: EBITDA up 15% on benign pulp prices and mix shift; Chemicals: Specialty chemicals margin pressured by ECH input costs; Cement: EBITDA/ton INR1,253 (highest ever) due to fuel/logistics efficiency

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: INR4,000cr dividend from UltraTech; INR2,880cr reinvested in Aditya Birla Capital to maintain 52.3% stake; final dividend of INR10/share (500%) paid; remaining cash used for growth capex in paints and Pivot; no share buybacks announced

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Cellulosic Fibres: expanding Lyocell capacity at Harihar, Karnataka by a combined 165K TPA -- an existing 55K TPA expansion plus a newly approved 110K TPA tranche backed by more than Rs 3,000 crore of additional investment -- taking total Lyocell capacity to 210K TPA by 2030; the business also targets overall CSF capacity of ~1 million TPA by 2028 with a higher share of specialty fibres. Building Materials (Paints, Birla Opus): commercialised its sixth and largest plant at Kharagpur in October 2025, completing a pan-India network of 6 plants with total capacity of 1,332 MLPA (~24% of organised decorative paints industry capacity), backward integrated with in-house emulsion (376.5 MLPA) and resin (92.6 MLPA) manufacturing; FY26 capex of Rs 550 crore took cumulative project spend to Rs 9,902 crore, completing the greenfield build-out on time and without cost overrun; retail presence scaled via Birla Opus Paints Gallery to 1,200+ franchised stores across 700+ towns. Building Materials (Cement): group subsidiary UltraTech Cement crossed 200 MTPA total grey cement capacity in April 2026 (up from ~52 MTPA in 2011), becoming the world's largest cement company outside China, through a mix of organic expansion, acquisitions and operational focus. B2B E-commerce (Birla Pivot): platform build-out to 50,000+ SKUs sourced from over 1,000 leading Indian and global brands, with expanding logistics, lender and procurement partnerships. Group level: total consolidated capital expenditure of Rs 15,396 crore in FY26 with growth capex comprising 72%, following nearly Rs 74,000 crore invested across businesses over the preceding five years; a strategic capital commitment of Rs 2,880 crore was made to financial services subsidiary Aditya Birla Capital. Chemicals: inaugurated a new CPVC Resin facility during the year (detail truncated in source text).

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, ambitious, disciplined; strong focus on market share over short-term profitability; emphasis on long-term structural advantages (distribution, brand, integration); acknowledges inflation risks but remains bullish on India’s growth; tone is ‘calibrated optimism’

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- India's largest caustic soda producer with a pan-India presence across the chlor-alkali segment
- Leadership position in the domestic Cellulosic Staple Fibre market with exports to over 50 countries
- Integrated Cellulosic Fibres model anchored by captive dissolving-grade pulp from Harihar and scale advantages across four manufacturing sites
- Diversified portfolio across Cellulosic Fibres, Chemicals, Building Materials and Financial Services that lets cycles naturally balance out, shielding consolidated profitability
- Birla Opus paints network is backward integrated with in-house emulsions (376.5 MLPA) and resin (92.6 MLPA) manufacturing; commissioning of the sixth factory cut average logistics cost by over 30%
- Birla Opus R&D scale -- 14 dedicated labs at Taloja with a team of 100+ experienced scientists supporting portfolio expansion and cost leadership
- Track record as Aditya Birla Group flagship: revenue CAGR of 16% and total shareholder return of 15%+ over the last decade

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Raw material inflation (20-25% COGS increase) persisting; demand elasticity testing in H1 FY27; price hikes may slow contractor adoption; Birla Pivot’s unit economics still early-stage; regulatory risk in financial services; currency volatility; geopolitical disruption to crude/pulp supply

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Birla Opus’s 75% product superiority in blind tests is a hidden moat; PaintCraft’s 6-12 month EMI service is a defensible financial innovation; Birla Pivot’s integration with Grasim’s supply chain (cement, chemicals, metals) is an unreplicable moat; contractor loyalty via Opus ID app creates sticky ecosystem; 90%+ unaided brand recall in 2 years is unprecedented in Indian paints

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [B2B E-commerce] Birla Pivot revenue grew 75% YoY to Rs.2,548 Cr with "Q1FY27 annualized revenue run-rate (ARR) continues to trend above Rs.10,000 Cr." (an ARR, not an annual figure); "the business remains on track to achieve break-even by exit of FY27" - though on a QoQ basis "revenue moderated amidst elevated market volatility and inventory optimisation approach pursued by value-conscious customers".
- [Financial Services] Aditya Birla Capital's Total Lending portfolio (NBFC and HFC) was up 32% YoY to Rs.2,19,289 crore and Total AUM (AMC, life and health insurance) stood at Rs.7,52,745 crore; the D2C platform ABCD had "more than 12 million customer acquisitions" as of 30th June 2026, and Udyog Plus had ~2.42 million registrations with a portfolio of ~Rs.6,229 Cr.
- [Accounting restatement] Prior periods are "Restated as Aditya Birla Health Insurance Co. Ltd adopted Ind AS 117", affecting Q1FY26/Q4FY26 comparatives, net worth and adjusted PAT - so year-ago comparisons in this deck are not on the originally reported basis.
- [Vodafone Idea] The investment in Vodafone Idea is carried at Rs.4,797 crore at 30th June 2026 versus Rs.2,830 crore at 31st March 2026 in both the standalone and consolidated balance sheets - a non-operating holding whose carrying value moved materially in the quarter.
- [Overseas pulp integration] Backward integration into pulp sits in minority-held JVs consolidated on an equity basis: AV Group NB Inc. (Canada) 45%, AGAB (Domsjo) (Sweden) 33.3%, AV Terrace Bay (Canada) 40%, plus CSF JV Birla Jingwei (China) 26.6%.
